content:
As WhatsApp officially rolls out its username feature, the app now allows users to save contacts' usernames alongside their name and phone number. Here's the details.

A username field when adding new contacts is gradually rolling out to some WhatsApp users

While usernames are a common feature on most messaging platforms, WhatsApp has only recently begun to move away from relying solely on phone numbers to identify users.

WhatsApp previously launched a username reservation system, giving users the opportunity to claim their preferred usernames ahead of the feature's official launch to avoid impersonation scams.

A few weeks ago, WhatsApp began enabling the username feature for some iPhone users.

According to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now starting to add a username field when users add new contacts. The field appears between the name field and the phone number field.

WABetaInfo reports:

WABetaInfo noted that the username field appears to be rolling out simultaneously to some users on both the beta and stable versions of WhatsApp.

In the writer's testing with the latest stable version, although the field has appeared, entering an existing username still prompts the message "This username is not on WhatsApp."

Regardless, this marks another step forward for WhatsApp in catching up with its competitors, adding a basic feature that many felt should have been in place long ago.
